title: Opportunistic Prefill Congestion Control and Kernel-aware Batching
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Goal: Reduce tail latency on mixed short/long workloads by combining an opportunistic prefill admission controller, batch-shape-aware kernel selection hints, and decode-prefill scheduling heuristics. Motivation: recent incidents and benchmarks show a long-request tail (p95-p99) spike when short chat-prefill requests interleave with long-generation jobs. This ticket implements a controller that limits in-flight prefill work based on GPU kernel characteristics and observed KV cache pressure, plus a lightweight flow that can opportunistically consolidate very short prefill windows into micro-batches without hurting latency SLOs. Scope: 1) admission controller that reasons about (a) current decode queue length, (b) per-model kernel latency profile, and (c) KV cache reuse probability; 2) a batch-shape hint API between admission layer and kernel selector so the runtime can choose fused attention kernels for dense short sequences or fallback to memory-optimized kernels for long sequences; 3) prefill/decode scheduler changes to allow transient prefill prioritization for requests that are latency-sensitive and to throttle cheap background prefill jobs. Out-of-scope: full model re-architecting or new kernel implementations — we will rely on existing kernels and kernel metadata. Success metrics: reduce p95 tail by >=25% on mixed workload benchmark, no more than 5% regression in aggregate throughput, maintain <=50ms added scheduling overhead at admission time. Risk/trade-offs: tighter admission reduces throughput for large batch-y workloads; kernel hints add coupling between admission and kernel selector which increases surface area for regressions. We will gate changes behind runtime-1.22 feature flag and run canary in staged traffic.
comments: 2026-03-01 - Aisha: Created initial ticket after analyzing 2026-02 weekly SRE dashboard. Root cause correlates p99 spikes with prefill-heavy background jobs colliding with low-latency chat requests.

2026-03-03 - Marco: Prototype design doc (confluence) linked. Proposed 3-phase approach: (1) conservative admission limiter, (2) kernel hint API, (3) scheduler prioritization. Requested bench harness and synthetic mixed workload profile from Bench team.
2026-03-05 - Bench team (J. Ramos): Delivered mixed-workload benchmark config and baseline numbers (p95=420ms, p99=980ms on a4-40). Attached dashboard link.

2026-03-07 - Design review: Agreed to use additive admission budget per-GPU rather than per-model to simplify rollout. Concern: bursty arrivals might underutilize GPUs; plan to allow short burst tokens when observed latency remains under SLO.

2026-03-09 - Engineering: Implemented admission controller prototype (branch: feat/admission-opportunistic). Early microbench shows p95 down to 320ms but throughput dropped 8% for long-run throughput test.
2026-03-10 - PM (R. Singh): Requested experiments tuning burst token size and adding a fallback policy that disables strict admission for reserved/dedicated customers.
2026-03-11 - Kernel team (L. Park): Added kernel metadata endpoint to runtime (kernel_p90, memory_profile, supported_sequence_ranges). Kernel hint API v0 documented in Confluence.

2026-03-12 - Marco: Started A/B canary on 5% traffic for chat routes. Initial telemetry: p95 improved 28% on canary, p99 improved 22%, overall tokens/sec -3%. Monitoring alerts added for any decode queue growth >2x baseline.
Next steps: stabilize burst heuristics, add per-tenant config for strictness, prepare rollout playbook with rollback steps and SLO guardrails.
